title: Plants
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Science and Technology; not yet checked by a CBC Science and Technology teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Teach outside first: a potted bean seedling, the school hedge, a touch-me-not (Mimosa) plant if the school has one. The child looks for each sign of life on a real plant before naming it.

skills.key_step: The child checks a plant against the signs of life (grows, reproduces, removes waste, responds, dies) and says the plant is alive even though it does not walk.

floor.prerequisite: Can tell living from non-living things.
floor.question: Is a stone living or non-living?

representations: a real seedling and a stone side by side
a picture of a seedling bending to a window
a table: sign of life, what the plant does
steps: Name the signs of life one at a time.
For each sign, find what a plant does (it grows taller, makes seeds, bends to light).
Ask whether moving from place to place is needed: it is not.
Decide: a plant shows the signs, so it is alive.
contexts: bean seedlings on the classroom window sill
a touch-me-not plant folding its leaves

board.do: Draw a seedling in a pot by a window, bending towards it.

board.say: Why has the stem bent this way?

board.do: Wait for the child to say it turns to the light.
Ask what will happen to a bean seed kept in a tin if it is planted.

misconceptions.ask: Does a hen need to fly far to be alive? Does a plant need to walk?
misconceptions.repair: Living things grow, reproduce and respond. A plant does all of these without walking.

misconceptions.ask: What do plants give off into the air from their leaves?
misconceptions.repair: Plants remove waste: they give off oxygen and water vapour, and shed old leaves.

misconceptions.ask: What happens when you touch a touch-me-not leaf?
misconceptions.repair: Plants respond: leaves fold, stems bend to light, roots grow towards water.

listen_for: it does nothing in the tin
misconceptions.ask: If we plant the tin beans in wet soil, what will happen?
misconceptions.repair: A seed rests until it gets water and warmth. Then it grows, so it was alive.

checks.question: Name two signs that show a maize plant is alive.
checks.answer: any two of: it grows, it makes seeds, it bends to light, it gives off waste, it dies

checks.question: A learner says a mango tree is not alive because it never moves from its place. Is the learner right?
checks.answer: No: the tree grows, makes fruit and seeds and responds, so it is alive
checks.shows: moving about is not a sign needed

skills.key_step: The child matches each part to its job: roots hold the plant and take in water, the stem holds it up and carries water and food, the leaves make food using sunlight.

floor.prerequisite: Names roots, stem and leaves on a plant.
floor.question: Which part of a plant is under the soil?

representations: a whole bean plant pulled up gently
a drawing with the three parts labelled
a celery or a white flower stem standing in coloured water
steps: Show a whole plant and name the three parts.
Roots: hold the plant firm, take in water and mineral salts.
Stem: holds the plant up and carries water up and food down.
contexts: a sukuma wiki plant in the kitchen garden
a maize plant blown by the wind
a cut flower in a jar of coloured water

board.do: Draw a plant with roots, stem and leaves.
Draw arrows from the roots up the stem to the leaves.

board.say: What is moving up the stem?

board.do: Wait for the child to say water.

board.say: And what does the leaf make with sunlight?

misconceptions.ask: Where is the water a plant drinks: in the soil or in the air?
misconceptions.repair: Roots take in water from the soil; leaves make food.

listen_for: the stem just holds it up
misconceptions.ask: How does water from the roots reach the leaves at the top?
misconceptions.repair: The stem holds the plant up and carries water and food.

misconceptions.ask: What happens to a plant if all its leaves are cut off?
misconceptions.repair: Leaves make the plant's food using sunlight.

misconceptions.ask: Two plants, same soil, one kept in a dark box. Which grows well?
misconceptions.repair: Plants make food in their leaves with sunlight; roots take in water and mineral salts.

checks.question: Which part of a plant takes in water from the soil?
A plant kept in a dark cupboard turns yellow and weak, though the soil is good. Why?
checks.answer: Its leaves cannot make food without light
